title: Scalable Simulation of Quantum Dynamics on Topological Quantum Hardware
abstract: Quantum computers offer a significant advantage in simulating quantum systems compared to classical computers for certain problems, although most current applications are limited to calculating static molecular properties using hybrid quantum-classical hardware. In this work, we establish a framework for the representation of quantum dynamics in molecular and condensed matter systems, designed for execution on topological quantum hardware. By leveraging the non-Abelian braiding statistics of Fibonacci and Ising anyons, we utilize the Solovay-Kitaev algorithm to approximate unitary propagators for a range of systems. We demonstrate the efficacy of these algorithms across a hierarchy of complexity, from two-level systems and one dimensional double-well potentials to condensed phase spin-boson models, simple molecules, and molecular reaction kinetics. These algorithms provide a scalable and robust pathway for simulating many-body condensed phase chemical physics on fault-tolerant quantum devices.
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive framework to simulate complex quantum dynamics for molecular and condensed matter physics using topological quantum hardware. It achieves this by mapping time evolution operators onto non-Abelian anyon braiding operations, utilizing the Solovay-Kitaev algorithm for high accuracy. The methodology proves scalable, offering a robust pathway for simulating strongly correlated and non-equilibrium quantum systems on fault-tolerant devices.
main_problem: Establishing a scalable and robust framework for simulating quantum dynamics in molecular and condensed matter systems directly on topological quantum hardware.
main_result: The framework successfully demonstrates the ability to approximate complex quantum dynamics, including molecular kinetics and spin-boson models, using non-Abelian anyon braiding.
method: The core method involves approximating unitary time propagators using the Solovay-Kitaev algorithm by simulating quantum gates via the braiding of Fibonacci and Ising anyons.
model_or_system: The work applies to a hierarchy of systems, including two-level systems, double-well potentials, spin-boson models, and molecular reaction kinetics, all mapped onto the physics of topological quantum hardware.
key_observables: Position autocorrelation function, expectation value of sigma_z, vibronic spectra, and reaction rates (k(T)).
important_parameters: Topological anyon types (Fibonacci, Ising), target accuracy (infidelity), and system parameters like coupling strengths (J, epsilon).
main_assumptions: The fidelity of the simulation relies on the accuracy of the Solovay-Kitaev approximation and the underlying assumption of fault-tolerant topological gate operations.
figures_summary: Figures compare exact dynamics (solid lines) against results from topological braiding (scattered dots/dashed lines) for various systems, showing high fidelity across different physical regimes.
paper_structure: The paper develops a theoretical framework, starting with simple models (two-level systems) to demonstrate the core methodology (anyon braiding via SK algorithm), and then scales this approach up to complex condensed matter and molecular physics problems.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges the gap between theoretical quantum simulation needs (molecular/condensed matter dynamics) and the physical realization constraints of emerging quantum hardware (topological qubits).
